summary: Hyperfy is an open-source framework for building and hosting interactive three-dimensional virtual worlds that run in a web browser, and its authors still call it alpha (version 0.16.0). Each object in a world is an app that pairs a glTF model with a JavaScript script run in an isolated compartment on both the server and the clients, with PhysX physics, VRM avatars, LiveKit voice chat and WebXR for virtual-reality headsets. It also provides a world server with a database, real-time multiplayer over web sockets and its own .hyp file format for bundling an app with its assets. Payments, geospatial data and captured-scene formats are outside its stated purpose. It has no verifiable identity or credential format in this repository (consistent identity is sent to a connected Hyperfy service that was not read) and no real-world sensing for augmented reality, since the engine requests virtual-reality sessions only; travel between worlds is limited to opening a link. A trap for a standards audience: the scripting interface is documented as likely to break between versions, and the bundle format, blueprint data and packet set are project-specific with no conformance test, so interoperability today means matching this one implementation.
